text:
Whatever happens with Nikita Kucherov's trade request, and it has dominated the hockey news for more than a week, he is still playing like the best player on the ice. On Saturday in St. Paul he took nine shots, assisted on the Lightning's first goal, and finished it on an overtime power play at 3:23 to complete a comeback from 3-1 down in the third. Tampa Bay won 4-3 and has won three straight.

The Wild started as if they'd been waiting all week. Blake Coleman scored 55 seconds in, on a chance worth about 4 percent, and Maxim Shabanov backhanded in a power-play goal two minutes later. Then the game tilted and stayed tilted. Tampa Bay out-attempted Minnesota 83 to 42 and won every regulation period on expected goals (the quality of chances), 4.12 to 1.96 overall. Jake Guentzel's power-play slap shot late in the second cut it to 2-1, but Shabanov, the undrafted KHL import, made it 3-1 at 6:49 of the third with his second of the night.

That is where our win probability model had Tampa Bay at its lowest. Guentzel tipped in his second at 13:44, and Charle-Edouard D'Astous tied it on a power-play slap shot at 16:29, a goal that moved the Lightning from 9 percent to 48. Brayden Point assisted on both of those, the second his 700th career point. In overtime Calvin Pickard denied Guentzel on the biggest save of the night, and 12 seconds later Kucherov ended it on the power play.

Our numbers say the Lightning deserved this one 82 percent of the time, so the comeback was less a miracle than the scoreboard catching up. Pickard was solid, stopping 30 of 34, while Dennis Hildeby allowed three on 22 shots, about a goal worse than expected. The Wild's discipline cost them: 19 penalty minutes and three Tampa Bay power-play goals, the winner included.

For Minnesota, a three-game winning streak ends, but on a night without a goal from Kirill Kaprizov they still took a point from a team that badly outplayed them. For Tampa Bay, every Kucherov night now carries a second question. This one answered it the way the Lightning would like: he is still theirs, and still winning games.
headline: Kucherov, trade request and all, wins it in overtime
